text:
Cycling is cheap, healthy and clean, but many people do not dare to ride in busy cities, and this essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take to improve road safety for cyclists, focusing on protected infrastructure and on rules and behaviour.

To begin with, protected lanes and lower speeds are the most effective way to keep cyclists safe. Physical separation from traffic prevents collisions, while lower limits, priority at junctions and driver training reduce risk. A city that builds a lane with kerbs or barriers on a busy road, for example, sees a large fall in injuries among cyclists and an increase in the number who ride. Cycle routes should form a connected network so that riders are not forced to share dangerous junctions or roundabouts with heavy lorries. Speed limits of thirty kilometres an hour in residential streets give drivers more time to react and make crashes less serious. Good lighting and well-maintained surfaces matter as well.

In addition, authorities should improve rules and behaviour. Lights and helmets protect cyclists themselves, and campaigns can persuade riders to use them. Drivers should be taught to look for cyclists, to leave a safe distance when overtaking and to check before opening doors, and these rules should be included in the driving test. Large lorries can be fitted with mirrors and sensors that remove blind spots. Traffic signals can give cyclists a head start at junctions, and police should punish drivers who endanger them. Equally important, safe routes to schools encourage children to cycle from an early age. Safer roads encourage more people to cycle, which in turn benefits health and reduces pollution.

In conclusion, protected lanes, lower speeds and clear rules offer the most realistic way to improve safety for cyclists.

analysis.type_vi: Solutions: an toàn cho người đi xe đạp

plan.think: Mở bài nêu đi xe đạp rẻ, sạch nhưng nhiều người không dám; hai nhóm: hạ tầng bảo vệ; quy tắc và hành vi.

Làn bảo vệ, giảm tốc độ: tách vật lý; ví dụ thành phố làm làn có bờ hoặc rào trên đường đông giảm thương tích, nhiều người đi hơn; mạng lưới liên tục, không dùng chung ngã tư với xe tải; giới hạn 30 km/h; ánh sáng, mặt đường.

Quy tắc và hành vi: đèn, mũ bảo hiểm; tài xế nhìn xe đạp, giữ khoảng cách, kiểm tra cửa; đưa vào thi bằng; xe tải gương, cảm biến; đèn tín hiệu cho xe đạp; cảnh sát phạt; tuyến an toàn đến trường; lợi ích sức khoẻ, ô nhiễm.
Làn bảo vệ, tốc độ thấp, quy tắc rõ.
